stem: An infant with known airway malacia later develops an ongoing wet cough; which secondary problem can occur because of poor cough clearance?
explanation: Protracted bacterial bronchitis can occur in airway malacia because poor cough clearance leads to retained secretions and persistent wet cough.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because poor cough clearance in airway malacia can lead to retained secretions and secondary protracted bacterial bronchitis.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because exercise-induced asthma symptoms are a separate condition and are not the secondary complication described here.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because bronchiolitis from RSV reinfection is not the specific consequence of poor cough clearance in airway malacia.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because pleural effusion is not the expected secondary problem from airway malacia-related poor cough clearance.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because foreign body aspiration is not the secondary complication implied by poor cough clearance in airway malacia.
